trial_court: Family Court No.1, Jaipur in divorce petition No.192 of 2010
case_name: Shikha Jaiman vs Bal Kishan Jaiman

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Shikha Jaiman, daughter of Shri Kalu Ram Sharma
parties.respondent_defendant: Bal Kishan Jaiman, son of Shri Hanuman Sahai Jaiman

facts_of_case: The parties filed a joint application under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act. A consent decree was passed by the trial court on 03.12.2010. The petitioner moved an application to withdraw the consent, but the respondent claimed that the statement recorded on 23.11.2010 showed no objection to the decree.

legal_principles.principle: A consent decree cannot be withdrawn once it is passed.
legal_principles.held: Submission of the learned counsel for the appellant is that though the application for dissolution of the marriage was filed under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, the appellant had on 29.10.2010 moved an application before the learned Judge, Family Court for withdrawing the said consent on the application under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: A party's statement in court can be used to determine the outcome of a case.
legal_principles.held: It is not disputed that after the aforesaid statements the belongings of the appellant have also been handed over to the appellant by the respondent.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is not maintainable as it is barred by sub-section 2 of Section 19 of the Family Court Act, and the delay in filing the appeal is condoned.

use_for_drafting: condoning delay in family court matters
